newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU makes WTO new offer on financial services.
newsitem.headline: EU makes WTO new offer on financial services.

text.p: The European Union has submitted a new offer to the World Trade Organisation (WTO) in a bid to improve chances for a global agreement on a financial services treaty, European Commission (EC) officials said on Tuesday.
Trade officials from the 15-nation bloc approved the new package last week and submitted the offer to the WTO in Geneva on Tuesday morning.
The offer includes plans to remove a dozen so-called residual restrictions and reducing nine others in financial areas ranging from the Amsterdam stock exchange to Portugal's investment fund sector.
An EC official said the new offer comes on top of pledges already made to the WTO for further liberalisation of the EU's financial sector.

Nations interested in signing the financial services pact have until July 14 to present their market-liberalisation measures to the WTO if a deal is to be struck by the December 1997 deadline agreed by members two years ago.
The 12 restrictions being ended are are:
In Austria, the elimination of economic needs testing for the licensing of branches or subsidiaries of non-EU banks.
In Belgium, the end of the need for firms that trade in securities to be incorporated in Belgium.
In the Netherlands, scrapping of a requirement to establish a subsidiary in the EU to become a member of the Amsterdam stock exchange.

In Finland, elimination of authorisation based on national interest test for the acquisition of shares giving more than one third of voting rights in medium and large banks. Also, the end of a Finnish nationality requirement for directors of stock exchange brokerage firms and the elimination of certain restrictive establishment conditions for intermediation in securities and derivatives.
In Ireland, elimination of a bar on foreign banks opening representative offices.
In Britain, ending a need for companies wishing to act as gilt-edged market makers, primary dealers of treasury bills or stock exchange money brokers to be incorportaed nationally.

In Sweden, elimination of a discriminatory deposit requirement with the Central Bank for foreign companies engaging in security trading and ending the need for companies that offer securities custody, deposit or settlement services to become an account operating institution.
In Portugal, ending the neccessity by investment funds to invest in 25 government funds and the scrapping of prohibitions on residents to issue securities on foreign markets.
